review_notes: I read the whole file and compared its simp attributes with the sibling file LocallyInjective.lean. I also grepped for uses of imageSieve_app, pullback_imageSieve and imageSieve_apply across Mathlib. I did not run Lean. The `@[simps -isSimp]` on imageSieve looks deliberate, because the unfolded existential would otherwise leak into goals. app_localPreimage is already simp and has a sensible orientation. I considered making pullback_imageSieve simp, but it has a single downstream use (Sites/Point/Conservative.lean, via rw), so there is little evidence of benefit. The one finding is a medium-confidence case of a missing canonical simp lemma. It is not certain, since the only in-file use is a `rw`, which would not change if the attribute were added.

findings.excerpt:
theorem imageSieve_app {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) {U : C} (s : ToType (F.obj (op U))) :
    imageSieve f (f.app _ s) = ⊤ := by
findings.problem: This lemma gives the canonical normal form `imageSieve f (f.app _ s) = ⊤`, but it has no `@[simp]` attribute. The sibling lemma for locally injective morphisms, `equalizerSieve_self_eq_top`, is `@[simp]`. Because `imageSieve_apply` is generated with `-isSimp`, simp has no other way to simplify `imageSieve f (f.app _ s)`. The expression stays stuck, and callers must rewrite by name, as `isLocallySurjective_of_surjective` does with `rw [imageSieve_app]`. The LHS is already in simp-normal form, and the RHS `⊤` is smaller and is the target of the existing simp lemmas `Sieve.top_apply` and `J.top_mem`. Adding the attribute therefore cannot loop or cause unwanted expansion.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`: `@[simp] theorem imageSieve_app ... : imageSieve f (f.app _ s) = ⊤`. Keep `imageSieve_apply` as `-isSimp`. Then a goal such as `imageSieve f (f.app _ t) ∈ J U` can be closed by `simp [J.top_mem]`, or by `simp` once `top_mem` is available. The `rw [imageSieve_app]` in `isLocallySurjective_of_surjective` can stay or become `simp`.
findings.benefit: Users get the same simp behaviour for the surjective case as for `equalizerSieve` in the injective case. Goals involving the image sieve of a section in the image reduce to `⊤` automatically, without the user needing to know the lemma name.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma equalizerSieve_self_eq_top {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} {X : Cᵒᵖ} (x : ToType (F.obj X)) :
    equalizerSieve x x = ⊤ := by aesop
